basic_identification.sector_category: Food and Agriculture / Food Hygiene and Safety (approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council and finalized by the Food Hygiene, Safety Management and Other Systems Sectional Committee, FAD 15, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Food Hygiene, Safety Management and Other Systems Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard prescribes food safety and hygienic requirements for street food vendors, laying down control checkpoints, minimum hygiene practices, and an inspection checklist with grading criteria to govern both mobile and fixed street food operations across India and ensure safe food is served to consumers.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Food Safety and Hygiene Guidelines (Food and Agriculture / Food Safety)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice / Guideline. Since IS 16066 is a procedural code of practice rather than a direct consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp on its own. However, compliance with its checkpoints, water quality rules, and vendor checklists is strictly integrated into the mandatory licensing and registration regulations of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) under the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulation, 2011. Additionally, its audit checklist serves as the core evaluation tool used to certify 'Clean Street Food Hubs' under the national Eat Right India movement. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Establishes a systematic 'farm-to-fork' approach, outlining control checkpoints across the food chain to ensure all raw materials, ingredients, and pre-packaged foods are obtained from safe, registered suppliers.

Mandates that street food stalls, carts, or kiosks must be situated in clean environments, completely separated and located at safe distances from open sewers, open drains, public toilets, garbage piles, animal stables, or industrial pollution zones to prevent airborne or vector contamination.

Vending carts or kiosks must be constructed from clean, smooth, non-absorbent, and easily washable materials (such as stainless steel, laminated panels, or food-grade plastics). Stalls must be fitted with overhead roofs, canopies, or parasols to protect exposed food from rain, dust, and bird droppings.

Mandates that water utilized for preparing food, mixing beverages, washing raw ingredients, cleaning food contact surfaces, and washing hands/utensils must be strictly potable and meet the physical, chemical, and microbiological parameters specified in IS 10500.

Requires complete physical separation between raw food ingredients and cooked/ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross-contamination. Separate cutting boards, knives, and prep surfaces must be marked and maintained for raw meats/vegetables and cooked items.

requirements.requirement_type: Temperature Control during Storage and Holding
requirements.detail: Enforces strict temperature-holding thresholds. Perishable raw materials must be refrigerated below 5°C, and hot cooked food held for serving must be kept at temperatures above 60°C to inhibit bacterial proliferation.

Utensils, plates, and cooking equipment must be of food-grade materials, free from cracks, rust, or deep scratches. Strictly prohibits using newspapers, recycled printed paper, or toxic plastics for wrapping or serving food.

Food handlers must wear clean clothing, protective light-coloured aprons, and hair nets or caps. Hands must be thoroughly washed with soap and potable water before starting work, after using toilets, and after handling raw waste.
Strictly prohibits unhygienic personal habits at the vending site, including spitting, smoking, chewing pan or tobacco, nose-picking, and coughing/sneezing over exposed food.

Mandates that all food handlers undergo periodic medical examinations to certify they do not suffer from skin infections, open cuts, discharging wounds, tuberculosis, cholera, or any other communicable/foodborne diseases.

requirements.requirement_type: Sanitary Waste Disposal and covered bins
requirements.detail: Separate, leak-proof, covered trash bins must be provided on or near the vending cart to collect wet (biodegradable) and dry (non-biodegradable) waste. Waste must be disposed of daily in designated municipal garbage bins, keeping the vending site clean and free of litter.

Provides a comprehensive, standardized audit checklist and grading sheet for local health authorities. Compliance scores are calculated to assign hygiene grades, supporting official sanitary certifications and clean-hub recognitions.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16066 : 2017 (First Revision) is the national Indian Standard establishing food safety and hygiene requirements for street food vendors. Developed by the FAD 15 Sectional Committee, this code of practice unifies safety guidelines for mobile and fixed street-vending operations across India. It mandates clean, covered cart designs, safe stall positioning away from sewers and garbage, the exclusive use of IS 10500-compliant potable water, and strict personal hygiene (including hair nets, aprons, and health certificates). By separating raw and cooked foods, prohibiting unhygienic practices, enforcing covered waste bins, and introducing a standardized audit checklist, the standard serves as the technical baseline for certifying clean street food hubs under FSSAI's 'Eat Right India' initiative.
